 More than 2.3 million Michigan voters cast ballots ahead of Election Day
 By
 Paula Wethington 
 Paula Wethington 
 Web Producer 
 Paula Wethington is a digital producer at CBS Detroit. She previously held digital content roles at NEWSnet, Gannett/USA Today network and The Monroe News in Michigan. She is a graduate of the University of South Carolina.
 Read Full Bio 
 Paula Wethington 
 Updated on: November 2, 2026 / 2:04 PM EST 
 / CBS Detroit
 Add CBS News on Google 
 Nearly 1 in 3 registered voters in Michigan had cast ballots as of Monday morning, with the midterm election entering its final stage. 
 While Tuesday is officially Election Day , Michigan has seen increased popularity in recent years of absentee voting and the newer option of early in-person voting.  
 Michigan reached 31.2% voter turnout as of Monday morning, with 2,313,165 ballots cast among 7,420,172 registered voters, according to the Michigan Secretary of State's office. This includes 1,569,715 absentee ballots and 743,450 early in-person ballots submitted. 
 The numbers for advance voting could still increase slightly, once final tallies are in.
 FLINT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 01: A ballot is dropped off in a drop box before Tuesday's general election on November 01, 2026, in Flint, Michigan. 
 Spencer Platt / Getty Images
 Absentee ballots can be returned until close of polls at 8 p.m. local time on Tuesday. 
 And while most early in-person voting sites wrapped up on Sunday, local clerks could extend early voting into Monday. The city of Detroit is among the 13 communities that continued early in-person voting into Monday. The others are Delhi Charter Township, Lansing, Taylor, East Lansing, Erie Township / Luna Pier, Flint Township, Grand Blanc Township, Harrison Township, Lincoln Park, Sterling Heights / Utica, Thornapple Township and Van Buren Township.
 "If you were not one of the over 2 million voters who already cast a ballot, be sure to check your polling location at mi.gov/vote and come out to vote on Election Day," Deputy Secretary of State Aghogho Edevbie said. Polling places will be open in Michigan from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time on Tuesday. Most of Michigan is in the Eastern time zone, a few counties in the Upper Peninsula are in the Central time zone.
 If the trend of absentee voting participation near or even surpassing Election Day turnout continues, the state could easily see 60% or more overall voter participation for the midterm election. 
 The August 2026 state primary election saw an overall voter turnout of 35% among its 7,359,855 active registered voters, the Michigan Secretary of State office said . This includes 1,569,715 absentee ballots returned and 743,450 early ballots cast. There were 1,057,836 ballots cast on Election Day. 
 The November 2024 presidential election saw an overall voter turnout of 77.9% among its 7,3190,017 active registered voters, state officials said. This was a record-voter turnout year in Michigan. The number includes 2,232,721 absentee ballots returned and 1,214,391 early ballots cast. There were 2,244,123 ballots cast on Election Day.
